gaps.sentence: You'd better ___ a taxi or you'll miss the plane.
gaps.explanation: had better takes the bare infinitive: you'd better take.

gaps.sentence: They're planning ___ the flat before selling it.
gaps.explanation: plan + to-infinitive (plan on + -ing also occurs informally): planning to redecorate.

gaps.sentence: We mustn't miss ___ this exhibition — it ends on Sunday.
The children were excited ___ the circus.
gaps.explanation: 'Excited to see' — the to-infinitive follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: It was kind of them ___ us a lift to the station.
gaps.explanation: 'It was kind of them to give …' — to-infinitive after the adjective.

gaps.sentence: I can't wait ___ you the photos.
gaps.explanation: can't wait + to-infinitive: can't wait to show.
fail takes the to-infinitive: failed to meet.

gaps.sentence: She was on the verge of ___ up her job to sail around the world.
gaps.explanation: 'On the verge of' ends in a preposition, so the gerund follows.
